matched_declared_lamp_baseline.resolved_2026_08_24: Checked and confirmed clean: recovered per-example ground truth by regenerating the deterministic lamp eval set (same seed 20260812) and joining on example_id against the saved step130_eval_progress.json (272KB, pulled from Drive: multidomain-stage3-v1/step130_eval_progress.json) -- sanity-checked to reproduce 86/100 exactly before trusting the split. Dark-truth answer_correct 42/50 (84.0%), Lit-truth 44/50 (88.0%) -- essentially balanced, slightly favoring Lit if anything. Does NOT carry the severe undeclared-test asymmetry. The bias is specific to the undeclared/self-invention condition (inventing a code AND committing to a final answer with no externally-anchored mapping), not a general lamp-domain answer-generation bias -- when the mapping is supplied, direction doesn't matter.

checkpoint130_comparison.description: Checkpoint 130 (latch multi-domain), same declared-mapping control task, for comparison against the base control above. No answer_is_code_word_rate value: the notebook that would have computed it (stage35_declared_mapping_control.ipynb) was built but never executed.

conclusion: Base and latch-adapted checkpoint 130 are similarly poor across all four jointly-measured metrics (adherence, accuracy, structure, global consistency). The latch adapter did not erase a strong pre-existing transfer capability; multi-domain training design is supported. Two threads opened: checkpoint-500 stability (04_stability_investigation) and directly amplifying the model's rare invention successes via SFT (05_self_bootstrapping).
